title: flow graph
description: The routing of one harness flow as data: which agent each node dispatches, where each of its outcomes routes, which counter a revision loop increments and what fires when that counter reaches its cap. The walker resolves the values here; the dispatch prompts stay in the flow's instruction core. This schema checks shape only: reachability, capped FAIL cycles, known run-mode and ledger ids, and agreement with the core are checked by scripts/check-flow-graph.sh, because JSON Schema cannot express them. Every <…> binding is named here and resolved by the flow's mode fork, never by this file.

formatVersion.description: Version of this graph format. A change to the key set raises it, so a walker never routes on a graph whose shape it does not know.

flow.description: The flow this graph routes, named as its instruction family (task_plan_writing for plugin/instructions/task_plan_writing_instructions_core.md).

description.description: What the graph routes and what it leaves in the instruction core.

start.description: The node a fresh run enters at.

entries.description: Every node a start may name as its entry, the graph's own start included. A walk continued from its saved state resumes at its pending node and names none of these; any node not listed here is refused as a start entry.

cap.description: The value at which an incrementing edge stops routing and takes its onCap edge instead. Agreement with the cap the instruction core states is checked by scripts/check-flow-graph.sh, not here.

counters.description: The loop counters, by name. An edge's increment and reset name one of these; the heartbeat's {iteration} is the counter of that name.

paths.description: Named run-artifact path templates, with {state_dir} and {branch} resolved by the walker. An escalation's evidence names one of these as the file the operator is pointed at.

reports.description: The report slots a run fills in. An edge's report names slots from this list; the walker prints one report: line per slot recorded, in this order, at the terminal node.

nodes.description: Every node of the flow, by id. A dispatch node sends one agent out and routes on what it returns; a terminal node ends the graph by handing off to its binding.

bindingName.description: A mode-contract binding, named and never resolved here: <ask> puts a question to the operator and resumes at a named node, <escalate> stops the run and reports why, <terminal_handoff> ends the graph and hands the run to what follows the flow.

kind.description: dispatch sends an agent and routes on its outcome; terminal ends the graph.

agent.description: The agent definition this node dispatches, by its name: field.

heartbeat.description: The line printed before every dispatch of this node. It carries {iteration}, so a stalled loop is visible from the heartbeat alone.

prompts.description: The dispatch prompt variants this node has in the instruction core. An edge's prompt selects one of them for the next dispatch.

findingsFolder.description: The folder this reviewer's findings are written to. Agreement with the folder the instruction core names is checked by scripts/check-flow-graph.sh, not here.

skip.description: Evaluated in order before the node dispatches; the first entry whose condition holds routes to its to without dispatching.

propertyNames.description: What the dispatched agent returned: returned (a writer finished), PASS / FAIL (a reviewer's verdict), questions (it needs an answer), no_ui (nothing to test), error / blocker (it could not proceed).

outcomes.description: Where each outcome routes. An outcome the agent returns that is not listed here is a fault in the graph, never a fallthrough.

construct.description: The phase is off in the adopter's configuration: the node never runs and its report slot records a skip.

phase.description: The phases toggle whose false value skips this node.

construct.description: The run mode excludes this node: it is treated as passed, not skipped, and its report slot says so.

runModeId.description: The run-mode directive id that excludes this node. Its vocabulary is owned by plugin/instructions/run_mode_instructions.md and checked by scripts/check-flow-graph.sh, not enumerated here.

report.description: The report slots this route fills, each with the status it records.

to.description: The node this outcome routes to.

increment.description: The counter this route increments. It requires onCap, so every incrementing route says what happens at the cap.

reset.description: The counter this route resets to its start value.

prompt.description: The prompt variant the target node is dispatched with.

ledger.description: The flow-progress ledger entry this route records. Its vocabulary is owned by plugin/instructions/autonomous_pause_and_ledger.md and checked by scripts/check-flow-graph.sh, not enumerated here.

onCap.description: The escalation taken instead of routing when the incremented counter has reached its cap.

binding.description: The binding this outcome hands the run to instead of routing to a node.

resume.description: The node the run resumes at once the question is answered. Required: an ask with nowhere to resume strands the run.

reason.description: Why the run stops: a counter reached its cap, the agent errored, or it returned a blocker.

summary.description: The operator-facing sentence, with {cap} resolved to the counter's cap.

roundCounts.description: The dispatch nodes, by node id, whose findings-folder round counts a cap escalation reports. The walker reads each one's findingsFolder, so each must name a dispatch node that carries one; a node the walk recorded as skipped is omitted.

evidence.description: The paths entry naming the file the operator is pointed at.
